details:
NISAR Wildfire Explorer is an interactive web application developed to explore wildfire-related surface changes using satellite radar observations. Using NASA–ISRO NISAR Level-2 GCOV L-band data, the application allows users to examine radar backscatter measurements across different observation dates and compare HH and HV polarizations.

The project focuses on the September 2026 wildfire in Aksu, Antalya, Türkiye. It provides interactive backscatter maps, temporal change visualizations, statistically unusual change indicators, and an optional external wildfire perimeter overlay. Users can explore how radar observations differ before, during, and after the fire-period observation.

By making satellite radar data more accessible and easier to investigate, the project demonstrates how space-based Earth observation technology can support the exploration of environmental changes associated with wildfires. It is designed as an exploratory tool, not an automated burned-area detection system, since radar changes can also result from factors such as soil moisture, vegetation, and surface conditions.
